papers.title: Nyx: a flexible framework for sleep scoring across species, lifespan and modalities.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Nyx is an unsupervised sleep-scoring framework based on principal component analysis that flexibly clusters epochs into sleep states. Validated on ~8,000 hours across 19 datasets, it generalizes across species, lifespan, modalities, and altered sleep architectures, matching human inter-scorer agreement and enabling real-time closed-loop manipulation.

papers.title: Sleep architecture and lying behavior in horses across age groups and two housing systems: an overnight non-invasive EEG study.
papers.summary: This study used a non-invasive EEG mask to compare sleep architecture and lying behavior in horses across age groups and two housing systems (communal stable vs. individual stalls) over four nights. Horses in the single stable setting showed increased REM sleep and lying-down frequency over time, while those in the large barn had longer lying episodes, and younger horses exhibited more REM sleep and complete sleep cycles than older horses.

papers.title: State-dependent aperiodic EEG dynamics track cortical network reorganization in chronic epilepsy
papers.summary: This study examined aperiodic EEG activity in a genetic mouse model of chronic epilepsy, finding steeper aperiodic exponents in epileptic mice compared to controls, which persisted after removing interictal discharges. The exponent varied with brain state and was influenced by pathological waveform shape during seizures, indicating both network reorganization and spectral distortion contribute to aperiodic changes.

papers.title: Investigating the Influence of Anti-Seizure Medications on Aperiodic EEG Activity
papers.summary: This study investigated the effects of lamotrigine and levetiracetam on aperiodic and periodic EEG activity in healthy volunteers. Results show that lamotrigine reduced aperiodic offset and exponent during eyes-open, while levetiracetam reduced exponent only, and both drugs altered periodic power in specific bands, suggesting aperiodic measures may reflect ASM neurophysiological effects.

papers.title: Diphenhydramine Disrupts Sleep Architecture in 5XFAD Alzheimer's Disease Model and Wild-Type Mice.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study tested chronic diphenhydramine (DPH) treatment on sleep architecture in 5XFAD Alzheimer's disease model mice and wild-type littermates using EEG/EMG telemetry. DPH fragmented NREM2 sleep in both genotypes, increased NREM1 and REM during the active phase, and exacerbated NREM2 fragmentation in 5XFAD mice, questioning its use as a sleep aid in AD.

papers.title: Neural and behavioral correlates of consciousness: the welfare consequences of fatal hypobaric and hypercapnic hypoxia in laboratory mice.
papers.summary: This study compared brain activity and behavior during fatal hypobaric and hypercapnic hypoxia in mice using EEG. Hypobaric hypoxia produced an early shift to delta frequency bands, suggesting an anesthetic-like state before loss of posture, potentially offering a more humane euthanasia method.

papers.title: Propofol-Facilitated Recovery Sleep Modulates Cognitive Function via Slow Oscillation-Spindle Coupling After Acute Sleep Deprivation in Rats.
papers.summary: This study investigated the effects of propofol-facilitated recovery sleep on cognitive function after acute sleep deprivation in rats, focusing on slow oscillation-spindle coupling. Propofol restored spatial and recognition memory, increased slow oscillation density, and improved phase-accurate SO-spindle coupling aligned to the up state, alongside a reduced NKCC1/KCC2 ratio.

papers.title: The Human Intracerebral EEG Platform: A Cloud-Based Trusted Research Environment for Collaborative SEEG Research in Epilepsy and Neuroscience.
papers.summary: This paper describes the development and implementation of the Human Intracerebral EEG Platform (HIP), a cloud-based Trusted Research Environment for collaborative stereo-EEG (SEEG) research. The platform provides secure access, standardized BIDS-iEEG data organization, collaborative spaces, and analysis software, currently hosting 34 institutions and 10 projects.

papers.title: Neural Signatures of Conscious Experience During Sleep: A Serial Awakening Study Using High-Density EEG
papers.summary: Using high-density EEG and serial awakenings in 140 participants, the study identified neural signatures of dreaming during NREM sleep. Dreaming was associated with reduced alpha/delta power and increased gamma measures posteriorly, and machine learning classifiers reached an ROC-AUC of 0.80, revealing reproducible posterior electrophysiological markers of consciousness.

papers.title: A Resource-Efficient CNN-Based EEG Auditory Attention Decoding ASIC
papers.summary: This paper presents a resource-efficient ASIC for real-time EEG-based auditory attention decoding, integrating a quantized CNN inference engine and Pearson-correlation classifier. Implemented in 22-nm CMOS, it achieves 0.4941 mW power and 7.34 ms latency, providing an energy-efficient platform for hearing-assistance applications.

papers.title: Decoding silent reading from non-invasive EEG
papers.summary: This study decoded silent reading from non-invasive EEG using a contrastive decoder, achieving above-chance word-level retrieval across a large vocabulary. The decoding scaled with data volume and was partly dependent on occipital electrodes, showing that lexical information is recoverable from EEG during reading.

papers.title: From Scalp to Source: Precise Phase Retrieval of Intracerebral Epileptic Sources Based on Surface EEG
papers.summary: This study validated the Gabor-Nelson dipole estimation method for reconstructing deep-brain phase from scalp EEG, comparing it to MRI-informed inverse solutions. GN achieved comparable phase accuracy without anatomical imaging, supporting its use for non-invasive seizure phase tracking and closed-loop neuromodulation.

papers.title: Generalizability of EEG-Based Dementia Classifiers: A Multicenter study of Alzheimer's, MCI, And FTD.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This multicenter study evaluated EEG-based machine-learning classifiers for dementia subtypes (CN, MCI, AD, FTD), addressing imbalance and cross-center generalizability. CN vs AD showed robust cross-center performance, while CN vs MCI and FTD contrasts were heterogeneous and limited, emphasizing the need for strict validation and uncertainty quantification.

papers.title: Atieh Schizophrenia EEG, a novel high-quality dataset designed to advance biomarker and machine learning research.
papers.summary: This paper introduces ASEEG, a resting-state EEG dataset from 101 subjects (51 with schizophrenia, 50 controls) recorded with 19 channels at 500 Hz, including eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions. It aims to support biomarker and machine learning research in schizophrenia.

papers.title: Interpretable machine-learning for depression classification based on a three-component EEG marker.
papers.summary: This pilot study developed an interpretable machine-learning framework for depression classification using a three-component EEG marker (coherence heterogeneity and asymmetry variability). RBF-SVM achieved AUC 0.910 under subject-wise validation, with SHAP identifying gamma-band coherence and beta asymmetry as key contributors.

papers.title: EEG-Based Effective Connectivity for Automated Detection of Major Depressive Disorder.
papers.summary: The paper proposes an automated MDD detection framework using graph-theoretical features from phase slope index (effective connectivity) and weighted phase lag index (functional connectivity) across five frequency bands, evaluated with machine learning classifiers. Results showed comparable classification performance for both connectivity measures, with delta and beta bands most discriminative, and EC offering additional interpretability via directionality.

papers.title: Time-frequency characteristics of scalp high-frequency oscillations provide complementary biomarkers in infantile epileptic spasms syndrome.
papers.summary: This study analyzed scalp high-frequency oscillations (HFOs) in infantile epileptic spasms syndrome (IESS) patients, comparing groups with hypsarrhythmia and interictal epileptiform discharges. HFO detection rates were significantly higher in hypsarrhythmia groups, with lower-frequency HFOs in hypsarrhythmia with ES, suggesting scalp HFOs as complementary biomarkers for assessing ictal states.

papers.title: Multidimensional Microstate Alterations and Interpretable Classification of Electrical Status Epilepticus During Sleep Using Multi-Channel EEG.
papers.summary: This study developed a microstate-centered multidimensional EEG framework to distinguish ESES patients from non-ESES epilepsy patients, revealing alterations in microstates B and C including prolonged duration, altered frequency, and reduced frequency chaos game representation entropy. A five-feature logistic regression model achieved promising exploratory discrimination, suggesting ESES involves more constrained and less flexible microstate dynamics.

papers.title: Event-Wise Stability of Patient-Specific EEG-MEG Deep Learning Spike Detection in Clinical MEG
papers.summary: This study developed a patient-specific EEG-MEG deep learning detector for interictal epileptiform discharges and evaluated event-wise stability across models. Adding EEG to MEG improved event-wise positioning, while MEG remained dominant in MEG-dominant cases, supporting multimodal patient-specific detection.

papers.title: Altered early cortical EEG maturation and its relationship to language development in Down syndrome
papers.summary: This study analyzed longitudinal resting-state EEG from children with Down syndrome and typically developing children, finding altered maturation of aperiodic and periodic spectral features in Down syndrome. In Down syndrome, a spectral dimension was associated with verbal developmental quotient rather than chronological age, indicating altered relationship between cortical organization and language development.

papers.title: Distributed EEG power asymmetries across frequencies in PTSD: Introducing the dynamic EEG power differential (DEPD) index.
papers.summary: This study introduces the Dynamic EEG Power Differential (DEPD) index to quantify distributed, frequency-specific hemispheric power asymmetries. Using resting-state EEG in PTSD and controls, they found that distributed inter- and intra-hemispheric power differentials, especially non-frontal and non-alpha, better distinguished PTSD and correlated with symptom severity than conventional frontal alpha asymmetry.

papers.title: Brain-Behavior Relationships in Children With ADHD: Resting-state EEG Networks Underlying Executive Function and Neurological Soft Signs.
papers.summary: This study examined sex-stratified brain-behavior relationships in pediatric ADHD using resting-state EEG graph-theoretical connectivity measures, finding sex-specific network alterations: lower local connectivity in ADHD girls and right centro-temporal inhibitory-circuit deficits in boys versus antero-posterior sensory-gating alterations in girls. Brain-behavior correlations emerged density-dependently, particularly in upper alpha and beta bands in ADHD girls, potentially explaining diagnostic camouflage.

papers.title: Seizure Onset Zone Localization in Drug-Resistant Epilepsy Using Self-Supervised Learning on Stereo-EEG
papers.summary: Developed CSOPE-Net, a self-supervised CNN-Transformer encoder for seizure onset zone (SOZ) localization from stereo-EEG. Achieved ROC-AUC 0.854 in cross-validation, 0.935 on held-out good-outcome subjects, and 0.822 on external cohort, also identifying SOZ-like contacts in poor-outcome patients.

papers.title: Neurocognitive Recovery After Liver Transplantation Is Driven by Metabolite-mediated Reactivation of Cortical Networks.
papers.summary: This prospective study of 21 liver transplant patients found significant neurocognitive improvements and EEG changes (increased alpha1/beta power, enhanced connectivity, altered microstate dynamics) post-transplant, alongside reduced plasma GFAP and elevated S-methyl-5'-thioadenosine (MTA). In vitro and in vivo experiments showed MTA attenuates inflammatory neurotoxicity and preserves neuronal function, suggesting a role in neuroprotection and cognitive recovery.

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of a novel digital cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia application versus zolpidem: An exploratory randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: This exploratory randomized controlled trial compared a 5-week digital cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (dCBT-I) app with zolpidem in 24 patients with chronic sleep-onset insomnia. Both interventions improved sleep onset latency at Week 5 with no significant difference, but dCBT-I showed sustained improvement at Week 10 follow-up while zolpidem showed slight recurrence.

papers.title: Machine learning to detect intraoperative ischemia from electroencephalography in carotid endarterectomy surgery.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study evaluated machine learning models for detecting cerebral ischemia during carotid endarterectomy using quantitative EEG features. Random forest achieved highest sensitivity and area under precision-recall curve, while XGBoost showed highest specificity; alpha-band activity and hemispheric asymmetry were most discriminative.

papers.title: Engineering a Timing-Accurate VR-EEG-Oculomotor Fusion System for Objective Assessment of Executive Function in ADHD.
papers.summary: The authors developed a timing-accurate VR-EEG-oculomotor system for the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test and validated stimulus-onset timing. In 101 children (64 ADHD, 37 control), a deep neural network fusing task performance, head rotation, eye movement, and N2/P3 ERPs achieved 83% accuracy in classifying ADHD, demonstrating multimodal integration for objective assessment.

papers.title: Visuomotor mismatch EEG responses over occipital cortex of freely moving human subjects.
papers.summary: This study combined wireless EEG with a VR headset to test for visuomotor mismatch responses in freely moving humans. They found robust mismatch responses in occipital cortex with reversed polarity and higher power than visual and oddball mismatch responses, analogous to those in mice.

papers.title: Left-sided Inhibition Deficit and right-sided Hyperexcitability in Treatment Resistant Bipolar Depression: A TMS-EEG study
papers.summary: This TMS-EEG study compared short-latency intracortical inhibition in treatment-resistant bipolar depression and healthy controls. It found reduced left-sided inhibition and right-sided hyperexcitability in patients, with right-sided global SICI partly normalized by lithium.

papers.title: EFS-NET: EEG-fNIRS multi-scale fusion network based on spatial calibration.
papers.summary: The paper presents EFS-Net, an end-to-end multi-scale fusion network integrating EEG and fNIRS for hybrid brain-computer interfaces, using spatial calibration to align delayed hemodynamic responses. On two public datasets, it achieved classification accuracies of 77.71% and 81.69%, surpassing state-of-the-art unimodal and traditional fusion models.

papers.title: Evaluating the performance of EEG based on ANN to predict the effectiveness of tDCS combined evaluative conditioning on obsession symptoms reduction in contamination OCD patients: Secondary analysis of data from a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: This secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial used EEG features and artificial neural networks to predict the effectiveness of tDCS combined with evaluative conditioning in contamination OCD patients. The optimized feedforward network achieved an RMSE of 0.57, indicating feasibility of predicting individual Y-BOCS score changes from pre-intervention EEG.

papers.title: EEG-ECeG Coherence Mapping of Human Cerebro-cerebellar Projections: An Exploratory Study.
papers.summary: The authors recorded EEG and electro-cerebellogram (ECeG) during finger movements in six healthy adults and used wavelet coherence to map cerebro-cerebellar connectivity. They observed movement-related delta/theta coherence patterns consistent with crossed cerebro-cerebellar projections, supporting the utility of ECeG for non-invasive imaging.

papers.title: Dynamic Hemispheric Lateralization of Naturalistic Emotional Processing After Unilateral Stroke: An EEG Study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 15 left-hemisphere stroke, 15 right-hemisphere stroke, and 15 healthy controls, the authors examined dynamic hemispheric lateralization during naturalistic emotional processing using EEG. They found that parietal-theta lateralization index dynamics differed by hemisphere group, with right-hemisphere patients showing increased switching and entropy during positive clips, suggesting a stability-flexibility imbalance.

papers.title: HD-tDCS modulation of the DLPFC-HPC-EC pathway to enhance working memory in schizophrenia: a TMS-EEG Study.
papers.summary: This randomized sham-controlled trial tested a single session of HD-tDCS targeting the left DLPFC in schizophrenia patients. It significantly improved working memory accuracy and reaction times, with TMS-EEG showing reduced excitability in EC and HPC, and mediation analyses implicating the DLPFC-HPC-EC pathway.

papers.title: EEG Connectomics in Rotator Cuff Injury: Central Network Reorganization During Three-Plane Antagonistic Shoulder Tasks.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.summary: This study characterized central nervous system reorganization in rotator cuff injury during three-plane antagonistic shoulder tasks using EEG connectomics. They found frequency-specific over-integration/under-segregation in beta and low-gamma bands and robust classification (ACC≈0.86) using graph metrics.

papers.title: Effects of exercise interventions on EEG alpha power across different populations: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 13 randomized controlled trials (497 participants) found that exercise interventions were associated with greater EEG alpha-band power than control conditions (Hedges' g = 1.23), but with considerable heterogeneity and wide prediction intervals, indicating substantial uncertainty across settings.

papers.title: Electroencephalography reveals late-stage modulation of stereoscopic object processing by naturalness and real-world size.
papers.summary: This study investigated how object naturalness and real-world size affect stereoscopic object categorization using behavioral and EEG measures. While early ERP components showed no differences, multivariate pattern analysis revealed distinct neural representations emerging around 600 ms, indicating that these high-level attributes modulate later integrative processing stages.

papers.title: Separating early and intermediate vision EEG signatures of facial emotion recognition in a fast divided attention task to eye and mouth features.
papers.summary: This study investigated EEG signatures of facial emotion recognition under fast divided attention to eye and mouth features. They found that the N170 and P250 components were modulated by emotional expression, while the P100 was not.

papers.title: Wavelet-based assessment of postural stability in young female volleyball players using a baroresistive platform.
papers.summary: This study used wavelet analysis to evaluate postural stability in young female volleyball players using a baroresistive platform. They found discriminative properties in frequency ranges associated with visual and vestibular control.

papers.title: ICE Catheter as Transesophageal Probe in Children With Congenital Heart Disease Undergoing an Electrophysiology Study.
papers.summary: This case series describes the use of an intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) catheter as a transesophageal probe in six infants and young children with congenital heart disease undergoing electrophysiology studies. The technique provided high-quality anatomical guidance and avoided large-bore venous access.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
